Chapter 2: BPS Perspectives on IEEE 1547-2018 Clauses
BPS Perspectives and Recommendations
• The “shall-trip” allowable clearing time ranges have been increased significantly in IEEE 1547-2018 to
enable DERs to utilize their capability to ride through abnormal voltage and frequency conditions on the
distribution system typically encountered during BPS contingency events.
• The RC and the area EPS operator should mutually agree on shall-trip settings in IEEE 1547-2018 to
ensure that both distribution system and BPS reliability needs are met. Ideally, “shall-trip” settings
should be chosen based on regional BPS reliability studies.

and III to begin their proceedings.
• DERs may cease to inject current during the permissive operation region of Category I and II. This
operation region is similar for momentary cessation, and many DERs will operate in it during BPS fault
events. DERs assigned to category III are required to ride-through voltage dips below 0.5 pu in
momentary cessation mode.
• AGIRs should ensure that DER operation in the permissive operation and momentary cessation region is
coordinated between the area EPS operator, the DER operator, and the RC and BA to ensure appropriate
performance from these resources during BPS fault events.
• Regional BPS reliability studies can help build an understanding of the impact of DER ride-through
operation, including the impact of momentary cessation on the BPS.
 DER response during fault conditions is not covered by 1547-2018, and these BPS reliability
studies should focus on ride-through capability of the DER. Dynamic voltage support capability
is likely limited from DER and would need separate language, clauses, etc. in any proceeding
from an AGIR.

740 involved about 150 MW of DER tripping on “Vector Shift protection” that exceeded six degrees.86

773 restoration efforts (and should be coordinated with the BA) where it is critical to maintain balance between load and
774 generation while system inertia is still relatively low. Increasing the penetration of DERs compliant with IEEE 1547-
775 2018 reduces this potential impact by requiring that DERs to be capable of ramping up their power output over a
776 prescribed period with a default of five minutes. Small DERs are allowed the option of utilizing a random delay,
